summary: This sermon explores contemplative prayer as a practice of resting in God's presence without agenda or words. Drawing on Jesus' invitation to his stressed disciples to 'come away to a lonely place and rest,' the pastor teaches a four-step rhythm (pause, surrender, contemplate, receive) for being with God amid the anxiety and busyness of modern life.
key_points: Jesus' response to his disciples' stress was an invitation to rest in his presence
We live as functional atheists, rarely acknowledging God's presence in daily life
Four steps: pause (find quiet space), surrender (lay anxious thoughts at Jesus' feet), contemplate (meditate on God), receive (rest in his presence)
The reward of private prayer is God's presence itself, not merely answered petitions
This is an invitation to abundant life, not a religious requirement
big_idea: Jesus invites us to find soul-level rest not through more religious activity, but by pausing to be with Him in His presence.
title: PRAYER: Be With God
